name: Blackjack
author: ChuckBuilds
description: Deals one hand of Las Vegas blackjack per rotation. Cards slide in and flip face up a few seconds apart, the player follows basic strategy, the dealer plays the house rules, and the hand ends on a BLACKJACK! / BUST! / PUSH banner. Every hand comes off a real shuffled shoe, so no two rotations are the same.

versions.notes: The hooks now match what the core actually does. One hand per turn: the 3.x controller draws a turn's first frame before it resets the cycle, and the plugin dealt on both, so every turn threw away a hand unseen and was timed from it -- the finished table could sit frozen for seconds, and the RUN OF n streak counted hands nobody saw. A turn now keeps the hand its first signal dealt, in either order. max_duration_seconds (and the device-wide dynamic duration limit) is a real cap: the controller treats get_display_duration as a floor that beats the cap, so a slow hand ran straight past it; a hand that would outlast the cap now plays faster, every beat in proportion, and still ends on its result inside it. display_duration is read: with dynamic duration off it is the slot length (22s by default) instead of the length of the discarded hand. Vegas: fixed mode deals the next hand each time the marquee comes round rather than showing one result all session, and a hand the ticker has shown is not then played on the panel. Static mode can no longer promise to play the hand out -- the marquee draws a paused plugin once and sleeps, which left an empty table up for the whole pause -- so it now stops the marquee on a freshly dealt, finished hand for result_seconds. Setting random_seed back to 0 now returns the shoe to system entropy without a restart. Floor raised to 3.2.0, the first core that reads a plugin's needs_high_fps; on 3.0 and 3.1 the deal ran at one frame a second. 3.0 and 3.1 report their version as 1.0.0 and predate floor enforcement, so no core can use this floor to refuse them; it records the requirement, which the README now states.

Static-analysis findings from the merge. Three were real: the Vegas width hook was reached through a getattr/callable dance that an analyser could not narrow, and is now a plain call with the AttributeError caught for cores that predate the hook; a walrus in an engine test bound a name nothing read; and a test imported a symbol it never used. The other ten were seeded random.Random calls flagged as weak crypto -- deliberate, since a fixed seed is what makes tests, goldens and preview renders reproducible, while the shoe a player is dealt from uses SystemRandom. Those are annotated with a B311-scoped nosec and a note in each module. No behaviour change.

The Vegas marquee now gets a summary of the finished hand -- the final cards with the result beside them -- instead of pausing for twenty seconds. 1.1.0 declared STATIC, which was better than being reduced to one frozen frame but stops a continuous scroll dead every time the plugin comes round. The hand is simulated to completion before the first card is dealt, so the finished table and its result are known at any instant and can be drawn as a still. Where the panel is too narrow to put the result beside the cards it goes over them, using the hand's own final-frame treatment; the threshold is measured, because the ticker crops anything wider than one panel to its start and that would keep the cards and lose the result. vegas_mode: static restores the pause-and-play behaviour.

Vegas marquee support, as STATIC only. A plugin that declares no Vegas mode is not skipped by the marquee -- it has one frame of its display() captured and scrolled past, which for a clock is right and for a twenty-second hand is a single frozen still, often a card halfway through its slide. STATIC pauses the marquee and lets the hand play. SCROLL and FIXED_SEGMENT are not offered because both want the content handed over as an image to be moved, and a hand is not an image; offering a vegas_mode override would only let someone pick the frozen frame.

Initial release. One hand of blackjack per rotation off a persistent multi-deck shoe, played by Vegas basic strategy against a dealer who stands on soft 17 by default. Four-colour deck (red hearts, gold diamonds, green clubs, indigo spades) on a lit felt table -- an ordered dither against a radial falloff, so the weave is densest under the cards and thins to black at the edges -- with a crimson-and-gold card back. Each seat reads as one line: name, hand, total. Rare hands announce themselves on the result banner (777, 21 IN 3, CHARLIE, DEALER n, BOTH 21, and a session win streak) before the score counts up. The deal, the hole-card reveal, a bust and a natural each get a beat of their own, and a hand ends with a tinted flash, a rattle and a spark burst on a win -- all of it a pure function of elapsed time, with no animation state anywhere. Card faces are a centred 5x7 rank at every size a real panel produces, with a pip-count sprite tier held back for cards larger than any of them, because counting pips across a room is slower than reading a numeral. The table lays itself out from the panel shape rather than a size whitelist, stacked normally and dealer-left/player-right on strips wider than 5:1. Dynamic duration is on by default, so the rotation lasts exactly as long as the hand does.
